scope: Final bounded session-token correction; security signer, normal access JWT middleware, two production issuer paths, focused tests. No commits, pushes, deployment, dependencies, CI, migrations, frontend edits or Learn.

findings.disposition: Corrected in frozen source; independent recheck and qualified production review remain required
findings.before: Remembered durable session expiry is 30 days but signRefreshToken always emits the default 7-day JWT. Company-context reissuance recomputes default lifetime relative to switching time.
findings.after: Refresh signer requires a supplied durable expiresAt and emits numeric exp equal to its floor in seconds. Initial session issuance signs the expiry returned by INSERT RETURNING. Context selection/return signs the original locked session expires_at without extending or shortening its durable lifetime.
redEvidence: remembered token exp differs from durable by 23 days
actual HTTP refresh on simulated day8 returns401 for a still-live remembered session
context switch token exp differs from original durable expiry
greenEvidence: ordinary/remembered JWT exp equals stored session expiry
real HTTP remembered refresh works on simulated day8 and rejects at stored expiry
selection and personal context return retain durable expiry and session identity
revoked/database-expired session rejects an otherwise unexpired remembered JWT

findings.disposition: Corrected in frozen source; independent recheck and qualified production review remain required
findings.before: Valid normal access JWT without SID uses a users-only lookup and bypasses durable session revocation/expiry.
findings.after: Normal access JWT requires a nonempty string SID and a live unrevoked unexpired session for its subject. Session validity is checked against clock_timestamp(). Separate existing scoped partner API-key branch is preserved.
redEvidence: actual HTTP /api/auth/session accepts a sessionless signed JWT with200 instead of401
greenEvidence: sidless JWT rejects before and after logout while valid bound JWT succeeds before logout
missing, wrong-account, revoked and expired session IDs reject

accessProduction: /company-context passes verified refresh proof.sid matching authenticated live durable session
refreshProduction: issueSession passes expires_at from persisted INSERT RETURNING
/company-context passes original session expires_at from locked current session
testCallers: company-invitations session helper updated to supply inserted expires_at
issuerAudit.verification: rg -n signRefreshToken/signAccessToken across apps/api/src and apps/api/tests; final signRefreshToken call-site search found no unconverted production/test callers
issuerAudit.libraryGrounding: Installed jsonwebtoken README supports direct numeric exp payload and prohibits combining it with expiresIn; no library change needed

environment.isolation: Unique temporary PostgreSQL schema cloned from public schema, with isolated synthetic records; cleaned after each process
environment.execution: require_escalated actual Node --test and real loopback HTTP. No fake database/request wrappers. Date.now is temporarily advanced only within serialized isolated lifetime tests to exercise JWT expiry through HTTP; restored in finally/cleanup.

diffCheck.command: git diff --check -- [five final auth source/test files]

verification.outputRead: Full red and green output read. Green synthetic insert/write/provider errors are expected failure-case checks, not unresolved test failures.

limits: No application-security or production-readiness claim; qualified human review remains required for authentication changes.
Previously issued JWTs keep their embedded expiration until replacement; no migration or retroactive token modification was performed. Existing sidless access JWTs now require reauthentication.
JWT exp uses standard integer seconds, so a token may expire less than one second before the millisecond durable expiry.
Actual provider staging/live Supabase, real browser/cross-tab behavior and full financial/API suite remain outside this increment.
Prior AUTH03 artifact auth.routes hash is superseded by this final snapshot; earlier focused behavior was rechecked by the green affected-auth run.
Other agents may modify unrelated root-owned code; hashes bind only the listed final auth files and evidence logs.
